title: What’s on upstream leaders’ minds? | Wood Mackenzie
gist: Simon Flowers reports that upstream oil and gas leaders are the most confident in a decade after the Iran war and the Strait of Hormuz closure pushed Brent to an average of US$100/bbl. Wood Mackenzie estimates this gives upstream and integrated companies at least US$700 billion of extra free cash flow in 2026. He sees resilient demand into the 2030s, a need for 20 million b/d of new supply by 2035, scarce deepwater rigs, the return of exploration and M&A (with deals priced at US$65-75/bbl plus contingent payments), and possible IOC access to Saudi Arabia upstream.

themes.theme: War windfall and the price outlook

insights.claim: Wood Mackenzie calculates that upstream and integrated oil companies will collectively earn at least US$700 billion of additional free cash flow in 2026, thanks to high oil and LNG prices and very strong refining margins, with Brent averaging US$100/bbl versus a notional US$60/bbl expected before the Iran war.
insights.so_what: Oil companies have a large cash windfall to fund buybacks, M&A and new projects.
insights.locator: The massive financial windfall from global conflict
insights.speaker: Simon Flowers

insights.claim: Simon Flowers argues that shocks and uncertainty are the new normal: the Iran war and Strait of Hormuz closure will not be the last disruption to energy flows, near-term price forecasting is well-nigh impossible, and volatility is the one certainty for oil and gas prices.
insights.so_what: Positions should be built for persistent oil and gas price volatility rather than a single price path.
insights.quote: Volatility is the one certainty for both oil and gas pricing.
insights.locator: 1. Macro – this is the new normal
insights.speaker: Simon Flowers

insights.claim: The oil industry still considers US$70-75/bbl Brent (real) the price needed to incentivise new projects that offset natural decline, and long-term price views have changed little despite the war.
insights.so_what: Long-term planning prices stay well below spot, which limits overinvestment risk.
insights.locator: 1. Macro – this is the new normal
insights.speaker: Simon Flowers

insights.claim: Belief that oil and gas demand will stay resilient into the 2030s and beyond has strengthened, reinforced by the Iran war as a reminder of the energy system's reliance on molecules, making the global upstream outlook the most upbeat in a decade.
insights.so_what: Supports a longer duration for upstream equity valuations.
insights.locator: 2. Global upstream outlook the most upbeat
insights.speaker: Simon Flowers

insights.claim: Wood Mackenzie estimates 20 million b/d of new oil supply must be brought onstream by 2035 to offset declining fields, and importing governments' desire for supply diversity is driving renewed investment in legacy, emerging and new upstream provinces not seen since before 2015.
insights.so_what: A large investment requirement supports oil services and upstream capex.
insights.locator: 2. Global upstream outlook the most upbeat
insights.speaker: Simon Flowers

insights.claim: After a decade of operator cost pressure, oilfield service companies have underinvested in new capacity as old assets retire, so deepwater drilling rigs will become scarce and day rates could soar as upstream investment rises.
insights.so_what: Bullish for deepwater drillers and heavy-lift vessel owners because day rates have room to rise.
insights.quote: deepwater drilling rigs will become scarce and day rates could soar
insights.speaker: Simon Flowers

insights.claim: Operators will need to reinvent their supply chain relationships, with closer collaboration, to secure rigs and heavy lift vessels at reasonable prices; refurbishing old rigs may be a stop gap.
insights.so_what: Expect longer-term contracts and partnerships between operators and service firms.
insights.speaker: Simon Flowers

insights.claim: After a rocky decade that included dividend cuts at some European majors, bigger IOCs want all-weather portfolios that can pay dividends even at the cycle low, built on strict hurdle rates, diversification across geography and oil/gas/LNG, trading and risk management.
insights.so_what: Majors will prioritize dividend resilience, favoring capital discipline over aggressive growth.
insights.speaker: Simon Flowers

insights.claim: The energy crisis has clearly shown the value of refining within integrated oil companies' portfolios.
insights.so_what: Integrated majors with refining exposure have outperformed during the crisis.
insights.speaker: Simon Flowers

themes.theme: Return of upstream M&A and exploration

insights.claim: There are currently more buyers than sellers in upstream oil and gas, and completed deals are typically structured on a base case of Brent US$65-75/bbl plus an oil price-linked payment over a set period, showing value agreements are possible despite extreme price uncertainty.
insights.so_what: Contingent oil-price payments are the deal structure that bridges valuation gaps.
insights.speaker: Simon Flowers

insights.claim: Banks are busy with upstream deals, and Simon Flowers expects more transactions may flow after the US mid-term elections.
insights.so_what: Possible pickup in upstream M&A after the US midterms.
insights.speaker: Simon Flowers

insights.claim: Exploration is back, with big IOCs and NOCs reloading high-impact deepwater acreage for volume at scale, and West Africa, Latin America and Southeast Asia among the hot spots.
insights.so_what: Positive for companies with deepwater acreage and for seismic and drilling services in these regions.
insights.locator: 6. M&A, exploration, DROs all on the table
insights.speaker: Simon Flowers

insights.claim: The Middle East crisis is laying foundations for IOC access to more Discovered Resource Opportunities in the region, potentially including Saudi Arabia, where upstream has been off limits to IOCs, with US IOCs and perhaps Chinese NOCs that have strong government-to-government ties well positioned.
insights.so_what: A potential opening of Saudi upstream would be a major new opportunity for US majors.
insights.locator: 6. M&A, exploration, DROs all on the table
insights.speaker: Simon Flowers
